content.text:
I fixed the hydration warning from the issue. I checked it with a temporary jsdom test, since deleted: it failed without the fix and passed with it. The existing hydration and `compiler-sfc` suites (500 tests) still pass. I didn't run the playground reproduction itself.

**Cause:** when a `v-bind()` expression in CSS contains characters like `.` (here `props.backgroundColor`), the server writes the variable name escaped into the HTML, as `--<id>-props\.backgroundColor`. The client's CSS-var getter returns the plain name, `<id>-props.backgroundColor`. During hydration the "expected" style was built from the plain name, so it never matched what the server rendered. This only showed up when the child's root element had its own `:style` binding, because that's the only case where hydration compares the `style` attribute at all.

**Changes:**
- `packages/shared/src/escapeHtml.ts`: I moved the existing `getEscapedCssVarName` helper and `cssVarNameEscapeSymbolsRE` here from `compiler-sfc`, unchanged, so the runtime can use them.
- `packages/compiler-sfc/src/script/utils.ts`: now re-exports both from `@vue/shared`, so nothing that imports them breaks.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts`: `resolveCssVars` now escapes each variable name the same way before adding it to the expected style. Server and client then match.
